summary.headline: Infosys guides FY27 revenue growth to 1.5%-3.5% cc and margin 20%-22%, with FY26 growth at 3.1% and margin steady at 21%.
summary.overview: Infosys closed FY26 with 3.1% constant-currency revenue growth and Q4 growth of 4.1% year-on-year, with adjusted operating margin stable at 21% (Q4 at 20.9%). Large deal TCV was $14.9-15bn for FY26 (up 28%, 55% net new) but Q4 TCV of $3.2bn was sequentially lower after a mega deal in Q3. FY27 guidance of 1.5%-3.5% cc growth is below FY26 on a midpoint basis, with about 0.75%-1% drag from a European manufacturing client and a further 0.75%-1% from onsite mix reduction. Management cited AI-driven compression offset by AI services growth, and acquisitions (Stratus closed and included, Optimum and Versent JV excluded) are a further swing factor.

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.commentary: FY26 growth 4.4%, above company average; management expects growth acceleration in FY27 and is strategic AI partner for 18 of top 20 clients in the vertical.

segments.name: Energy, Utilities, Resources & Services (EURS)
segments.commentary: Expected to accelerate in FY27; 80% of FY26 large deal TCV was net new. Utilities demand driven by grid constraints and data center power needs.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Challenging, especially European auto; one large European manufacturing client ramp-down is worth 0.75%-1% of FY27 growth drag. Grew more than double company average in FY26 on large deal ramp-ups.

segments.name: Communications
segments.commentary: Grew more than double company average in FY26 on large deal ramp-ups; budgets flat to negative, discretionary spend constrained.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Consumer demand muted, discretionary budgets under pressure; clients expect AI-led productivity savings on similar budgets.

segments.name: Geography: Europe vs North America
segments.commentary: Europe grew faster than company average on mega deals (NHS, Liberty Global, manufacturing); North America share falling from about 57% to about 55% per Reuters' question, not disputed by management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance 1.5%-3.5% cc YoY; lower end assumes deteriorating environment, upper end assumes improvement. About 25 bps from Stratus (closed, included); Optimum and Versent JV excluded pending regulatory approvals.
Drag of 0.75%-1% from lower revenue from one European manufacturing client, including a deal not meeting return thresholds.
Further onsite mix reduction of 0.75%-1% in FY27; third-party cost expected at similar FY26 levels.

FY27 operating margin guidance 20%-22%, assuming wage hike, productivity pass-through and AI investment headwinds offset by Project Maximus. Acquisitions (Stratus, Optimum, Versent) add about 0.7% margin headwind on annualised full-year basis post-closure.
Effective tax rate FY27 expected at 29%-30%. H1 expected to be stronger than H2 per normal seasonality.
Plans to hire at least 20,000 freshers in FY27; no decision yet on wage hike quantum or timing.
capex_capacity: Utilisation excluding trainees 83% in Q4 and 84.4% for FY26; including trainees 81.1% for FY26, reflecting investment in future capacity.
Onsite mix 22.8% in Q4 vs 23.1% in Q3; exit trajectory already 40-50 bps lower and further reduction expected in FY27.
Subcontractor intensity expected to stay broadly flat near current levels in FY27, with a medium-term decline possible.
Over 90% of employees skilled on AI platforms; over 30,000 developers deployed on GitHub Copilot.
Cash and investments $4.5bn at year end after returning over $4bn to shareholders in FY26.
demand_pricing: Volumes flattish for FY26; growth driven by realisation gains, partly from Project Maximus. Management says pricing environment stable and AI revenue comes at better pricing.
Competitive intensity higher; management cites one competitor's unusual pricing on some deals but says it is not a broad trend.
Clients prioritising cost optimisation and productivity; management says productivity is passed through to clients on competitive deals, creating margin pressure.
Large deal pipeline described as strong; FY26 $50mn+ clients up by 3, $100mn+ clients up by 3, $400mn+ clients up by 2.
AI services growing faster than company average; management declined to disclose the AI revenue figure, saying only it is above the 5.5% of Q3 revenue cited earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of FY27 guidance and what do the acquisitions contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Stratus (insurance) is closed and contributes about 25 bps; Optimum (healthcare) and the Versent JV are pending regulatory approvals and are excluded. Management said acquisitions are not baked into the guidance and will be added upon closing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did headcount decline 8,000 QoQ and what is the hiring and wage plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower volumes and utilisation drove the quarterly decline; headcount grew 5,000 YoY. At least 20,000 freshers planned for FY27. No decision yet on wage hike quantum or timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower Q4 TCV a sign of AI deflation or client spend cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 included a UK mega deal; excluding it, numbers are comparable. Management noted slower decision making in March in some pockets but did not see a significant impact on large deal sign-ups.

qa_highlights.question: How much does AI-driven productivity compress the existing base, and is it accelerating?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competitive intensity is high and productivity discussions are built into multi-year deals; it did not quantify gross growth vs compression and said there has been no step change in the last two months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin walk in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Headwinds: 50 bps acquisition amortisation, 30 bps normalisation of Q3 one-off gain, 20 bps compensation costs. Offsets: 40 bps currency and 30 bps Project Maximus.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the FY27 guidance band 200 bps and what is the organic midpoint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said visibility is better than last year when a wider 3-point band was used; the midpoint of about 2.25% organic reflects a balance of AI services growth and net new deals against compression and the Europe manufacturing ramp-down.

risks_watch: AI-driven productivity pass-through and competitor pricing could extend compression beyond current assumptions; the guidance midpoint is below FY26 growth.
Regulatory approvals for Optimum and the Versent JV: timing uncertain, and their revenue and margin effects are excluded from guidance.
Ramp-down at one large European manufacturing client and the onsite mix reduction both weigh on FY27 revenue.
Wage hike timing and quantum not yet decided; margin guidance assumes its impact is absorbed.
Q4 large deal TCV fell sequentially; watch whether Q1 FY27 large deal wins and net new share recover.
Management declined to disclose AI revenue share; watch for any future disclosure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and large deals, cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly stressed that compression from AI productivity is real and the guidance is a balance of growth drivers against deflation. Evasive on AI revenue disclosure, wage hikes, and CEO succession.
key_quotes: We see growth which is not a compression.
We do not have a plan that the headcount will be less at the end of the year.
Overall at this point in time, the volumes for the last year has remained flattish.
So there, I mean, it is not that this is something widely prevalent.

growth.why: FY27 cc revenue guidance of 1.5%-3.5% (midpoint 2.5%) is below FY26's 3.1%, with a 0.75%-1% drag from a European manufacturing client and 0.75%-1% from onsite mix reduction; backing is partial (large deal TCV of $14.9-15bn in FY26 with 55% net new, ~25 bps from Stratus, Project Maximus pricing) but no specific capacity is being added.
